desc: secrets referenced without a dedicated environment

concrete.feature:
vulnerable-checkout-and-exfil:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # VULNERABLE: pull_request_target grants secrets access, and this step
      # checks out the PR head, i.e. attacker-influenced content, into that
      # privileged context. This is the exact anti-pattern GitHub's secure-use
      # docs warn about.
      - name: Check out PR head ref
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      # In a real attack, a step from the untrusted checkout (e.g. a script
      # committed on the attacker's branch) would run here with
      # DUMMY_API_KEY_DO_NOT_USE in its environment. We simulate that "attacker
      # script" step inline for lab clarity instead of shipping a second
      # malicious file, but the effect (secret read by code influenced by the
      # untrusted ref) is the same.
      - name: Simulate untrusted step reading the secret
        env:
          DUMMY_API_KEY_DO_NOT_USE: ${{ secrets.DUMMY_API_KEY_DO_NOT_USE }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p exfil-proof
          echo "Secret value observed by untrusted-context step: $DUMMY_API_KEY_DO_NOT_USE" > exfil-proof/proof.txt
          echo "This step ran with the PR head ref checked out and a repo secret in scope." >> exfil-proof/proof.txt

      # Sink: a GitHub Actions artifact. An artifact produced by a workflow
      # run triggered from a fork PR is visible to anyone who can read the
      # repo, which is itself a documented exfil path in GitHub's own docs.
      # This never leaves GitHub's infrastructure, unlike a curl to an
      # external endpoint.
      - name: Upload proof artifact (in-GitHub sink, no external destination)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: exfil-proof
          path: exfil-proof/proof.txt
